ADU218 watchdog trip-time measurement (WD1, documented 1 s)
==========================================================
Device: Ontrak ADU218, USB 0a07:00da
Witness: SDM4065A s/n SDM46A0CA00021 fw 0.0.0.20, on K0
Wiring: K0 load side -> DMM leads only. No load current.

Method: close K0, arm WD1, stay SILENT for exactly T, then read RPK0
once. That read ends the silence window, so RPK0 reports the state AT
T seconds of silence with nothing having refed the timer. One trial
per window; the window is re-established from scratch each time.

Why not poll: any command refeeds the timer (manual 6d, invalid
commands included), so polling would prevent the timeout under test.
Why RPK0 and not the DMM: a DMM read costs ~0.7 s, and that latency is
exactly what corrupted the earlier '3.7 s' figure.

  T (s)   RPK0 after T s of silence   WD    verdict
  -----   -------------------------   ---   -------
   0.40               1                1    closed (not yet)
   0.70               1                1    closed (not yet)
   0.90               1                1    closed (not yet)
   1.10               0                0    OPEN (tripped)
   1.40               0                0    OPEN (tripped)
   2.00               0                0    OPEN (tripped)

Bracket: still closed at 0.90 s, open by 1.10 s.
So the WD1 trip lies in (0.90, 1.10] s of silence.

=== independent corroboration of the tripped state ===
K0 re-closed, WD off:  RPK0=1  DMM: 6.1391 ohm (CLOSED)
WD1 armed, silent 2.0 s: RPK0=0  WD=0  DMM: overload sentinel (OPEN)
(DMM is on a separate bus and sends nothing to the ADU218, so reading
 it cannot feed the watchdog. It is the only independent evidence the
 contact physically moved.)

restored: WD=0 PK=000 DB=1

=== WD2 (10 s), 2026-08-27: does it trip on TIMEOUT or on ARMING? ===
Witness: SDM4065A, on K7 (TEST_RELAY default since 2026-08-27).
Standing DC volts before the run: 0.0004 V (leads dry, so the volts
gate cannot be masking a lead on a powered net).

The WD1 measurement above cannot answer this question, and neither
could the committed test. Both establish "armed, waited, contact
open" -- which is satisfied by two different hypotheses:

  H1  the relay opens when the timer EXPIRES        (the claim)
  H2  the relay opens as a side effect of ARMING    (would be useless)

At WD1 there is no room to sample between the two: one DMM read costs
~0.41 s and the whole window is 1 s. WD2 gives 10 s, so the contact
can be read EARLY, where H1 and H2 disagree.

Method: close K7, read the DMM continuously (it sends the ADU218
nothing, so it cannot refeed the timer), arm WD2, keep reading.

  t after arming (s)   DMM
  ------------------   ---
  0.00 .. 9.45         17.471 - 17.474 ohm   (24 readings, all CLOSED)
  9.86                 17.473 ohm            (last closed)
  10.83 .. 13.71       overload sentinel     (9 readings, all OPEN)

  read_watchdog()         -> 0     (self-cleared by the trip)
  read_watchdog_tripped() -> True

Bracket: still closed at 9.86 s, open by 10.83 s.
So the WD2 trip lies in (9.86, 10.83] s of silence, against a 10.0 s
nominal. The gap is one DMM read.

=> H1. The contact stayed closed for 9.86 s AFTER arming, across 24
   consecutive readings that vary by 3 milliohms. Arming does not
   de-energise; the timeout does.

The hardware test now uses WD2 for exactly this reason and asserts the
early sample, with a guard that the sample landed < 8 s after arming --
a slow VISA round trip would otherwise silently degrade it back into
the WD1 form. Proven by mutation both ways: opening the relay right
after arming (simulating H2) FAILS the WD2 test on the early assertion
and PASSES the old WD1 test. That is the coverage the change adds.

restored: WD=0, all relays de-energised.
